newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans drop sharply on slow exports-traders.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans drop sharply on slow exports-traders.

text.p: Lower-than-expected weekly export shipment figures from the U.S. Department of Agriculture pressured nearby soybean futures Monday, floor traders said.
USDA put export inspections at 8.9 million bushels. That figure fell below the low end of trade expectations for 10 million to 15 million bushels.
Some of the weakness in soybean futures also stemmed from a sharp drop in soymeal futures, traders said.
Heavy commodity fund selling pushed nearby soymeal futures down more than half the daily trading limit near midsession.
Refco, Rosenthal Collins, R.J. O'Brien and Smith Barney were noted sellers in the soymeal pit, traders said.

At 1100 CDT, soybeans were up nine to down six cents per bushel, with July down 5-1/4 at $8.40-1/2 a bushel. Soymeal futures were $0.90 higher to $4.20 per ton lower, with July down $4.20 at $269.30 a ton.
